1.note: The edition points לְשָׁמִים, "to (the) heavens". The sense is unclear; it may mean words worth lifting to heaven. It rhymes with חֲכָמִים and בְּשָׂמִים, and a reading close to "spices" may be meant.

2.note: "Linked poem" (shir nitsmad): the poem defines it in the next lines. Each pair of lines ends on the same word used in two senses (homonym rhyme, Arabic tajnīs). The prose speech that follows and the alphabet poems are built this way; the notes give the two senses.

3.note: Both lines end in תְּהִלָּתוֹ. Here the two senses are nearly the same ("praise"); the first may play on הלל "to shine" (His splendor). Hab 3:3 "and the earth was full of His praise".

4.note: גֻּלָּה is the bowl or knob of a crown or lamp (Eccl 12:6, Zech 4:2), and a spring of water (Josh 15:19 "springs of water").

5.note: תְּשׁוּבָה is "repentance" in the first line and "return" in the second. 1 Sam 7:17 says of Samuel "and his return was to Ramah" (הָרָמָתָה); here Ramah is read as "the height".

6.note: חֵמָה is "wrath" in the first line. The second uses Job 29:6 "when my steps were washed in cream (חֵמָה)", so the same letters mean "cream", an image of plenty.

7.he: הַנּוֹתֵן טוֹבַת הַיֵּצֶר פְּרִידָתוֹ. / וְחֶבְרַת הַיּשֶׁר פְּרִי דָתוֹ
7.note: Rendered by the sense "the good (against) the impulse is parting from it"; the syntax is compressed. The rhyme splits פְּרִידָתוֹ "his parting" into פְּרִי דָתוֹ "the fruit of his faith (law)".

8.note: תְּעָלָה is a water channel (1 Kgs 18:32) and a healing or new skin over a wound (Jer 30:13, 46:11).

9.note: אַשְׁפָּה is a dunghill (1 Sam 2:8 "lifts the needy from the dunghill") and a quiver; Lam 3:13 "He sent into my kidneys the sons of His quiver", that is, arrows. Here the man shoots at desire.

10.note: צִנָּה is a shield (Ps 91:4) and cold (Prov 25:13). "Its heat" (חֲמָתוֹ) is the heat of the troubles; the word also echoes חֵמָה "wrath" above.

11.note: מְרוּצָה is a running or race (Jer 8:6) and, from רצץ, crushing oppression (Jer 22:17 "oppression and crushing").

12.note: זִמְרָה is the choice produce of the land (Gen 43:11) and song or music (Exod 15:2).

13.note: This line has no partner line with the same end word; all the other lines of the speech come in pairs. A line may be missing in the source. שְׁאוֹן may also be the pit of Ps 40:3 (בּוֹר שָׁאוֹן).

14.note: יְחִידָה "only one" is a name for the soul (Ps 22:21). The difference between the two uses is not clear; the first may mean his solitude, or his life while the soul is still in him. Uncertain.

15.note: Near-homonyms: מְשׂוּכָּה "hedge" (Isa 5:5) and מְסֻכָּה "covering" (Ezek 28:13 "every precious stone was your covering").

16.note: תַּאֲוָה is "desire" in the first line and "boundary" in the second (Gen 49:26 "to the bound of the everlasting hills"; Num 34:7 "you shall mark out").

17.note: מָשְׁחָת "corruption, blemish" (Lev 22:25) and מִשְׁחָה "anointing"; same letters, different vowels.

18.note: מְסִלָּה is a highway (Isa 62:10 "clear it of stones") and, in 2 Chr 9:11, the terraces or steps that Solomon made for the house of the LORD.

19.note: הֵלֶךְ is a traveller (2 Sam 12:4) and a flow (1 Sam 14:26 "a flow of honey"). The world's pleasures should not tempt the wise man.

20.note: יוֹרֵהוּ from ירה: "shoots it" (with arrows) and "teaches him" (1 Sam 12:23 "I will teach you the good and right way").

21.note: אוֹר is "light" in the first line and "lightning" in the second, as in Job 37:11 "He spreads the cloud of His lightning".

22.note: צִיר is a messenger or envoy (Prov 25:13) and a pang or pain (Isa 13:8).

23.note: נֵזֶר is the Nazirite's separation (Num 6) and a crown (Ps 132:18 "upon him his crown shall flourish").

24.note: In the alphabet poems that follow, the two lines of each poem start with words that look or sound alike (sometimes one word split into two) and end with the same word in two senses. Each poem's lines begin with its letter. The alphabet is complete, Alef to Tav.

25.note: אֱמוּנָה "faith" and אֲמוּנָה "nursed, reared" (Lam 4:5). אֲסִירָהּ "her prisoner" and "I will remove her" (from סור).

26.note: Start: בּוֹחֵן "Tester" and בּוֹ חֵן "in Him is grace". End: בְּנִי "my son" and בְּ־נִי "into wailing" (נִי, lament, Ezek 27:32).

27.note: Start: גִּלְעָד "Gilead" and גִּיל־עַד "everlasting joy". End: גּוֹרֵשׁ "drive out" and "cast up" (Isa 57:20, the sea whose waters cast up mire and mud). The person of the first verb is compressed in the Hebrew.

28.note: Start: דּוֹר שָׁוְא "a worthless generation" and דּוֹרְשָׁיו "His seekers". End: דוֹרְךָ "your generation" and דּוֹרְכָה "bending (a bow)".

29.note: Start: הַצֵּל "save" and הַצֵּל "the shadow". End: הָרִיק "unsheathe" (Exod 15:9 "I will draw my sword") and הָרִיק "the empty".

30.note: Start: שָׁנִים "years" and שָׁנִים "scarlet" (Prov 31:21). End: חֲסִידָה "stork" and "pious (soul)".

31.note: Start: זְרַע "sow" and זֶה רַע "this is evil". End: זְרוֹעַ "sowing" and "arm"; the first line has the word twice, at the end of each half. The syntax of the second line (who reaps what) is compressed.

32.note: Start: חֲנִי־נָא "encamp, please" and חֲנִינָה "grace". End: חֲלִי לָהּ "a jewel to her" (Prov 25:12) and חֲלִילָהּ "her flute".

33.he: טוֹבְעִים / טוֹב עִם ... טָבְלוֹ / טוֹב לוֹ
33.note: Start: טוֹבְעִים "sinking" and טוֹב עִם "good with". End: טָבְלוֹ "his dipping" and טוֹב לוֹ "good for him".

34.note: Start: יִמָּאֲסוּ "are despised" and "melt away" (Ps 58:8, from מסס). End: יְקָר "precious thing" and "honor". The second half-line is compressed and the rendering is uncertain.

35.note: Start: כִּידוֹד "spark" (Job 41:11) and כִּי דוֹד "for an uncle". End: כְסוֹף "long for" and כְּסוֹף "like the end".

36.note: Start: לוֹחֵץ "pressing" and לוֹ חֵץ "it has an arrow". End: לְמַד "learn" and לְ־מַד "as a garment" (2 Sam 20:8 מַדּוֹ לְבֻשׁוֹ).

37.note: Start: מוֹרִים "rebelling" and "aiming" (from ירה, to shoot). End: מִדִּין "rich carpets" (Judg 5:10) and מִ־דִּין "from judgment".

38.note: Start: נְצַפֶּה "we look out" and "we overlay" (with gold). End: נְסוּכָה "poured out" and "woven, spread" (Isa 25:7 "the veil that is spread over all the nations").

39.note: Start: סוּגָה "hedged" (Song 7:3 "hedged with lilies") and "turned back" (from סוג, Ps 53:4). End: סוֹד "council" and "secret". Gen 49:6 "into their council let my soul not come".

40.note: Start: עָרֹם "naked" and עָרוּם "wise, crafty". End: עֲדֵה "adorn yourself" (Job 40:10) and "pass over" (Job 28:8 "the lion has not passed over it").

41.note: Start: פִּנָּה "he cleared" (Isa 40:3 "clear the way") and "cornerstone". End: פּוֹרֵק "throws off" (a yoke) and "tears apart".

42.note: Start: צָדוּ "they hunted" and "laid waste" (from צדה). End: צָפוּ "they flowed" (Lam 3:54) and "they watched". The second half of the second line is compressed.

43.note: Start: קְרָב "war" and קְרַב "draw near". End: קְלָעִים "slingstones" and "carvings" (1 Kgs 6:32 קִלַּע, carved with open flowers). The worldly house is the thing to avoid.

44.note: Start: רָאשִׁים "heads" and רָשִׁים "poor", which sound alike. End: רָדוּ "they ruled" and "they scraped out" (honey, Judg 14:9).

45.note: Start: שָׁעַר "weighed, reckoned" (Prov 23:7) and שַׁעַר "gate". End: שָׁמָּה "there" and שַׁמָּה "desolation".

46.note: Start: תֵּבֵל "world" and תֶּבֶל "perversion" (Lev 18:23). End: תִּכְלָה "end, limit" (Ps 119:96) and תִּכְלֶה "you cease". This is the last letter; the alphabet is complete.

47.note: נֶחְבְּאוּ "are hidden" sounds like his name חֶבֶר. Isa 11:12 "He will gather the outcasts of Israel and the scattered of Judah".

48.note: רוּחַ is "wind" (scattered to every wind) and "breath" (the breath of my mouth, Ps 33:6).
